title: Quiet Hours Respect the User's Timezone
userRequest: The server-side movement nudge computed its overnight quiet window in UTC. api/cron/movement-nudge.ts read one now.getUTCHours() for the whole scan and fed it to shouldNudge, but DEFAULT_QUIET_HOURS (21 to 8) is a LOCAL window. For a user in America/New_York the guard actually protected 5pm to 4am local: it silenced the evening nudge that should fire, and opened a 4am to 8am window where a push could wake someone up. Los Angeles was worse. A live production bug affecting every US user with server push enabled.
description:
Resolves the quiet-hours window in each user's own timezone instead of once in UTC for everyone.

localHourIn(timeZone, now) returns the wall-clock hour in a zone, and the cron now calls it INSIDE the candidate loop rather than computing a single module-level hour before it. That one move is the entire fix; the stale 'per-user timezone is a future refinement' comment is gone.

Intl was chosen over a stored UTC offset deliberately: an offset is wrong twice a year. The DST tests are what keep that decision honest — the same zone either side of both US transitions, asserting spring-forward skips 2am and fall-back repeats 1am. A fixed-offset implementation fails those. Also covered: the hour12:false midnight-as-24 trap (normalized with % 24), a half-hour offset zone (Asia/Kolkata) as a canary that the hour comes from the zone rather than arithmetic, and graceful degradation — a null or garbage identifier falls back to the UTC hour without throwing, so one bad row cannot abort the scan for every other user.

The zone rides in on the existing health heartbeat with no new transport. It is shape-validated at the boundary (timeZoneFrom, conservative IANA pattern, 64 chars) because the value is written to the database and later handed to Intl, so an unbounded client string has no business reaching either.

Two things the type checker caught that the plan did not call out: addPushToken constructs a PushRow directly and needed time_zone preserved, otherwise registering a second device would wipe the stored zone; and mirrorMovement must not let a null from an older client clobber a good stored value.

Schema note: account_push needs `alter table account_push add column time_zone text;` — documented in the api/_lib/account.ts header alongside the other DDL.
